subject: Re: Kickoff: behavioral dispositions eval for the assistant
body:
Status + one methodological risk to settle before the first gated report.

Done: migration finished ahead of Bao's deadline, harness onboarded 6/12 as replanned, and we've run four assistant candidates through the full 2,500-SJT battery. Results mirror the paper: all four are overconfident in low-consensus scenarios (they concentrate probability on one action where humans split), and the two smaller candidates deviate hard from high-consensus answers - one misses them 19% of the time, right in the paper's 15-20% band. The emotion-expression vs. composure pattern shows up too.

The risk: what counts as "failing" the gate. If we gate on matching the human preference distribution, we're baking 550 annotators' demographics into a launch blocker. I'd rather gate only on high-consensus misses and report distributional divergence as informational. This needs a product decision, not a stats one.

Csilla
